cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus, is writing a letter to the believers in Rome. He opens it the way you'd introduce yourself on a phone call to someone who doesn't have your number saved: name first, then what he does. He calls himself 'a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God'.
And this good news isn't a last-minute plan. Paul says God promised it beforehand, and it's written down in the Holy Scriptures.

cards.question: Paul says God promised the gospel beforehand in the Holy Scriptures. Who did God promise it through?
Paul says the gospel is about God's Son, who was a descendant of ___ according to the flesh.

cards.text: David, Israel's king, is the Son's family line on the human side. But Paul says that through the Spirit of holiness, He was declared with power to be the Son of God.

cards.question: How does Paul say God's Son was declared with power to be the Son of God?

answers.text: By His resurrection from the dead
By His teaching in the temple

cards.text: Then Paul gives Him His full name: 'Jesus Christ our Lord.' Through Him, Paul says, we received grace and apostleship, and friend, I've never heard a job title that came with grace stapled to the front.

cards.question: Paul says that through Jesus, we received grace and apostleship. What does Paul say it's for?

answers.text: To call the Gentiles to obedience from faith
To guard the Law of Moses in Jerusalem
To build a new temple for the church in Rome

cards.question: True or false: Paul tells the believers in Rome that they're also among those called to belong to Jesus Christ.

cards.text: Paul's introduction runs six whole verses before he gets to the 'To' line: all in Rome who are called to be saints. Friend, that's longer than my voicemails, and my voicemails run so long the phone hangs up on ME.

cards.question: Paul writes to all in Rome who are ___ by God.

cards.text: Then comes the greeting itself: 'Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.' Friend, every letter I open starts with 'FINAL NOTICE.' This one starts with GRACE.
With the greeting done, Paul gets going: 'First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you.' Before anything else, he's grateful.

cards.question: Why does Paul thank God for the believers in Rome?

answers.text: Their faith is being proclaimed all over the world
Their church is the largest one in the whole world
They sent money to pay for all his travels

cards.text: Paul says God is his witness that he remembers them constantly, in his prayers at all times. Friend, I can't remember where I put my oven timer, and this man remembers a whole church.

cards.question: When Paul prays for the believers in Rome, what does he keep asking God for?

answers.text: That by God's will he may come to Rome
That Rome's rulers would turn to God
That the church would grow in number

cards.question: Paul says he longs to see the believers in Rome so he can impart some spiritual gift to strengthen them. True or false: Paul says the encouragement would only go one way, from him to the believers in Rome.

cards.text: Paul wants them to know how often he's planned to come to them. And still, he hasn't made it to Rome.

cards.question: So why hasn't Paul visited the believers in Rome yet?

answers.text: He has been prevented until now
The church asked him to wait
He wanted to finish in Spain first

cards.text: He wants a harvest among them, just like he's had among the other Gentiles. Paul says he's obligated to Greeks and non-Greeks, to the wise and the foolish.

cards.question: Paul says he's obligated to Greeks and non-Greeks, to the wise and the foolish. Because of that, he's so ___ to preach the gospel to the believers in Rome too.

cards.text: Then Paul says it plain: 'I am not ashamed of the gospel.' Friend, I hide one lopsided cookie at the BOTTOM of the box, and this man puts it in WRITING for all of Rome.

cards.question: Why isn't Paul ashamed of the gospel?

answers.text: It is the power of God for salvation
It is the law of Moses for the Jews
It is the wisdom of the wise for all people

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the gospel's power for salvation is only for the Jews.

cards.text: Paul says that power is for everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek. EVERYONE who believes, friend.
Lean in, friend. Paul says the gospel reveals the righteousness of God.

cards.question: Paul says the righteousness of God comes by ___ from start to finish.

cards.text: Then Paul backs it up with Scripture from the prophet Habakkuk (Hab 2:4): 'The righteous will live by faith.' Start to finish, friend, every batch, not just the first one.

findings.problem: The earlier cards say only that the gospel was promised in Scripture; they give no basis for choosing David over Moses or Saul. This blank therefore asks for unseen wording rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The sentence makes David himself 'the Son's family line.' Romans 1:3 instead says that God's Son was a descendant of David according to the flesh. The card should preserve that relationship by saying that Jesus descends from David.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The setup mentions only that the Romans are called to be saints. It does not give the baker enough to reason out 'loved' rather than 'tested' or 'judged,' so the card asks for an omitted word from the unseen verse.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Verse 11's setup, Paul's longing to see the Romans and impart a spiritual gift, appears for the first time inside the choice question. No story card has set up this moment, and the preceding choice is about Paul's prayer request, so this cannot use the exception for a choice following another choice whose setup was already told.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card.
